topics.name: General World Model
topics.description: Integrated world-model frameworks combining world state, evolution, interaction, or observations; a system-level scope, not a quality ranking.

topics.name: Memory
topics.description: Persistent state, historical information, off-screen entities, identity, or memory consistency.

topics.name: Interactive
topics.description: Worlds that respond to user or agent actions and continue running.

topics.name: Real-Time
topics.description: Reported real-time generation, simulation, or low-latency interaction, with the original hardware and timing conditions.

topics.name: Acceleration
topics.description: Reducing inference, execution, or rendering time and computational cost.

topics.name: Long Video Generation
topics.description: Sustained or extended-duration video generation and its temporal consistency, beyond generic multi-step simulation.

topics.name: Streaming
topics.description: Incremental input, continuous output, or causal chunk-by-chunk generation; not automatically real time.

topics.name: Multi-Agent
topics.description: Multiple acting entities within the modeled world and their shared state or interactions; distinct from coding-agent collaboration.

topics.name: Action Control
topics.description: Explicit control of world behavior through keyboard, mouse, robot actions, or other action inputs.

topics.name: Physics
topics.description: Physical mechanisms, motion, contact, collisions, materials, or physical consistency.

topics.name: World Generation
topics.description: Creating scenes, assets, games, or simulation environments from desired specifications.

topics.name: World Reconstruction
topics.description: Recovering scenes, physics, or rules from reference images, video, trajectories, or observations.

topics.name: World Editing
topics.description: Editing objects, layouts, properties, behaviors, or world rules.

topics.name: Neural Rendering
topics.description: Neural image or video generation conditioned on code, executable state, geometry, or proxies.

topics.name: Planning
topics.description: Searching or imagining actions with world models to choose a plan.

topics.name: Agent Learning
topics.description: Using generated worlds, simulated experience, or world-model feedback to improve an acting or reasoning agent.

topics.name: Code Execution
topics.description: Modeling execution semantics, predicting computational states, or investigating execution correctness; not every method that runs code.

topics.name: Post-Training
topics.description: Fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, distillation, or adaptation of existing models.

topics.name: Benchmark
topics.description: Reusable test tasks and scoring protocols; a method-side benchmark does not automatically become the README category.

topics.name: Dataset
topics.description: Constructed or published world programs, scenes, trajectories, simulations, or paired data resources. Public release scope is recorded separately.

topics.name: Evaluation
topics.description: Focused evaluation, diagnosis, and analysis of capabilities, evidence, or failure modes.

topics.name: Survey
topics.description: Surveys, literature syntheses, taxonomies, and research overviews.

tracks.name: Code World Model
tracks.subtitle: Generate a world
tracks.description: Intent → executable state and rules → observations and interaction.
tracks.question: What should exist, and how should it evolve?

tracks.name: Code as Model
tracks.subtitle: Understand a world
tracks.description: Observations → executable hypotheses → prediction, intervention and verification.
tracks.question: What mechanism explains what we observed?

tracks.name: Related perspectives
tracks.subtitle: Clarify the boundary
tracks.description: Software execution worlds, alternative physical representations and streaming decoder infrastructure.
tracks.question: What is being modeled, and is the representation executable?

categories.name: Persistent & playable worlds
categories.question: Who owns state, rules and consequences outside the current frame?
categories.description: Explicit state evolution coupled to generative observations, world editing and gameplay.

categories.name: Code-guided video & rendering
categories.question: How does executable structure control appearance over time?
categories.description: Executable previs, proxy conditioning, neural rendering and causal streaming.

categories.name: Physical simulation synthesis
categories.question: Does generated code instantiate working physical mechanisms?
categories.description: Text-to-simulation, numerical engines, contact and dynamic scene construction.

categories.name: Scene & asset programs
categories.question: Can a scene be edited, composed and loaded into a simulator?
categories.description: Programmatic geometry, articulation, scene compilation and editable assets.

categories.name: Worlds for agent learning
categories.question: Can generated environments grow with an agent's capabilities?
categories.description: Runnable training environments, curriculum generation and environment–agent co-evolution.

categories.name: Inverse world reconstruction
categories.question: Which program and parameters explain the observations?
categories.description: Image/video-to-code, real-to-sim reconstruction and system identification.

categories.name: Executable physical reasoning
categories.question: Does running a hypothesis support quantitative predictions and interventions?
categories.description: Abductive world discovery, physical supervision and solver synthesis.

categories.name: Rule induction & planning
categories.question: Is the inferred transition function useful for choosing actions?
categories.description: Programmatic dynamics learned from trajectories or rules, followed by search or control.

categories.name: Verification & evaluation
categories.question: Can we distinguish a working world from a plausible-looking one?
categories.description: Executable benchmarks, physical obligations, functional tests and auditable critiques.

categories.name: Software execution worlds
categories.question: Is code the environment being predicted rather than a physical world representation?
categories.description: Learned execution, tool feedback and software-agent world models.

categories.name: Alternative representations
categories.question: What can language, constraints or neural priors supply without synthesized world code?
categories.description: Conceptual neighbors that clarify the scope of executable world representations.

categories.name: Streaming decoder infrastructure
categories.question: When can pixels be emitted after a latent arrives?
categories.description: Causal video decoding, cache reuse and deployment kernels supporting interactive renderers.

dimensions.name: Role of code
dimensions.question: What does the code actually do?

dimensions.name: Interaction contract
dimensions.question: What can a user or agent change?

dimensions.name: Evaluation target
dimensions.question: What has the paper chosen to measure?

reading_paths.title: From code to pixels
reading_paths.description: Executable previs, persistent state, then fast observation generation.

reading_paths.title: From observation to mechanism
reading_paths.description: Infer an executable explanation, then test its predictions and utility.

reading_paths.title: From plausible to executable
reading_paths.description: Separate visual quality from engine readiness, physical checks and task success.

reading_paths.title: Worlds that train agents
reading_paths.description: Move from generated environments to curricula and reusable experience.

collection_sections.name: Benchmarks & Evaluation
collection_sections.description: Compare the task, submitted artifact and evidence of success. These suites test different capabilities; their scores are not interchangeable.

collection_sections.name: Datasets, Harnesses & Streaming Systems
collection_sections.description: Reusable code corpora, construction workflows and systems that deliver persistent worlds or streaming pixels.

collections.name: Video reconstruction & inverse graphics
collections.question: What observable scene structure and motion survive video-to-code reconstruction?

collections.name: Procedural 3D creation & scene editing
collections.question: Does the delivered native scene satisfy the reference and preserve the intended structure?

collections.name: Physical mechanisms, parameters & solvers
collections.question: Does code recover the mechanism, satisfy physical checks and generalize beyond the observed motion?

collections.name: Executable interaction, state & intervention
collections.question: Can the world complete tasks, preserve state and behave correctly after an edit?

collections.name: Code-guided video generation
collections.question: How well does the rendered video follow the code-built spatial and temporal plan?

collections.name: Executable code & simulation corpora
collections.question: What reusable programs, paired observations and verification records are available?

collections.name: Construction & verification harnesses
collections.question: What execution and inspection loop helps an agent build a usable world?

collections.name: Streaming worlds, renderers & decoders
collections.question: Is the system expanding world state, generating observations, or only decoding latents?
